text:
marta: Observed a ~55-65% token/sec drop in prod after the scheduler change merged this morning (the handoff timing tweak). Rollout got auto-throttled.
kevin: ack, saw alerts. Is this only for high-fanout prompts or across the board?
marta: mostly traffic with lots of small conversations (avg seq len 32, many parallel requests). Larger single-session requests are fine.
sam: link to CI perf run: https://ci.internal/redwood/7890 — job shows throughput regression on staging too.
ci-bot: perf/regression-checker: job 7890 — 60% token/sec drop vs baseline (2026-03-18T09:12). See artifact: /artifacts/7890/perf-summary.txt
marta: quick numbers from prod window 09:00-09:20:
- baseline token/s: 12.4k
- after merge: 4.8k
- 95p latency increased ~1.6x
- kv cache hit rate down from 82% -> 34%
kevin: kv hit rate tanking smells like more short-lived shards or batch fragmentation. Any changes to handoff/stealing heuristics in the patch?
marta: yes, the patch reduces handoff wait from 5ms -> 0ms in many cases and adds more aggressive preemption. commit: github.com/redwood/serving@b3f9c2
li: can you paste a profiler snapshot? pprof or perf?
marta: pasted flame snippet (trimmed):
```
flamegraph: https://perf.redwood/fg/7890
top frames:
- scheduler::dispatch (40%)
- kv_cache::lookup (22%)
- continuous_batcher::coalesce_wait (18%)
- cuda_kernels::memcpy (6%)
```
kevin: scheduler::dispatch at 40% is suspicious — sounds like thrash during handoff where small batches keep being created/destroyed and KV cache entries churn.
sam: repro script (very noisy):
```
# simulate many small parallel requests
for i in $(seq 1 400); do 
  ./bench --concurrency 80 --seq 32 --qps 200 &
done
```
marta: repro on staging shows same drop. pprof shows a hot path in coalesce_wait where wait_for_handoff returns immediately and we reschedule, creating new batches prematurely.
kevin: hypothesis: removing the small delay increases number of tiny batches and reduces prefix sharing, which both decreases effective batch size and reduces kv_cache reuse. Also increases scheduler overhead.
li: bisect plan: revert the handoff timing commit on staging and run 15m perf check. I can run a quick binary revert job.
marta: before revert, one thing to try quick: raise batch_min_window from 2ms -> 6ms and see if that recovers hit rate.
sam: tried raising to 6ms on a canary node — kv hit rate climbed from 36% -> 78% and tokens/s recovered to ~11.8k in canary.
kevin: ok that points to timing. We should either revert the change or land a patch that increases the minimum batching window to avoid fragmentation.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: automatic rollout paused due to perf-slow alert. Deployment id: deploy-2026-03-18-15
deploy-bot: Rollout paused, canary nodes isolated. To continue either: revert commit b3f9c2 OR apply batch-window bump and redeploy canaries.
marta: opening PR to bump min window and add a feature flag: https://github.com/redwood/serving/pull/4123 — quickfix only, full scheduler refactor later.
li: ran bisect locally — culprit index: the change to immediate handoff + disabling the small-delay path. Repro commit: b3f9c2. Revert candidate: revert(b3f9c2) works.
kevin: action items:
- marta: land the temporary bump PR and enable feature flag off by default for now (PR 4123)
- li: prepare revert PR for b3f9c2 if the quickfix doesn't land fast enough
- sam: keep running staged perf checks and post numbers here
marta: landed PR 4123 to canary at 15:42, canary perf is green: tokens/s ~12.1k, kv hit 80%, 95p latency back in baseline.
sam: running full prod rollout in 10m with the flag on until we ship a proper scheduler fix.
kevin: follow up: we'll add a unit test for batch coalescing + a perf test in CI to avoid this regressing silently. Also add a trace point to record handoff churn rate.
marta: thanks everyone. keeping the rollout gated until we confirm 1h stable window.
deploy-bot: :thumbsup: rollout paused -> canary with fix -> scheduled prod rollout 16:05 if no regressions.
ci-bot: summary artifact: /artifacts/7890/perf-recovery-4123.txt
kevin: note for postmortem: include KV cache metrics (hit/miss), avg batch size, handoff count/sec, and scheduler dispatch CPU.%
marta: added a short replay script and notes to the PR describing how to reproduce (small concurrent seq workloads).
